paragraphs.text: Which was built by Nimrod, as Nineveh was afterwards by his nephew Ninus. {Gen 10:11} Of the greatness of this city, besides what we read in holy writ, much may be read in Herodotus and Pliny. It was the head city of the Assyrian and Chaldean monarchy, which lasted above seventeen hundred years, till Cyrus the Persian took the kingdom. Isaiah prophesied against it in several chapters. Habakkuk maketh it his whole business. Jeremiah had set forth how Sheshach, that is, Belshazzar, should drink the dregs of the cup of God’s wrath. {Jer 25:26} Here, and in the next chapter, he discourseth it more at large, showing how it was that Babylon was to drink of that cup; and for more certainty, it is spoken of in this prophecy as already done.
paragraphs.anchor: The word that the Lord spake against Babylon.

paragraphs.text: Let all take notice of the good news; there shall be a general jail delivery, sing therefore Io triumphe.
paragraphs.anchor: Declare ye among the nations.

paragraphs.text: So Isa 21:9.
paragraphs.anchor: Say, Babylon is taken.

paragraphs.text: This Bel was Nimrod, whose nephew Ninus set him up for a god. Merodach (a restorer of their empire, {a} whereof Nimrod had been founder) was likewise idolised. They are called "dirty deities" - foedites et stercora, a name good enough for them - and said to be confounded. See Isa 46:1. "Sorrows" also; because "their sorrows shall be multiplied that hasten after another God." {Psa 16:4}
paragraphs.anchor: Bel is confounded.

paragraphs.text: {a} Merodach σκηπρουχος sive Sceptrifer Chaldaica appellatione.

i.e., Out of Media and Persia, which lay northward from Chaldea. The Jews had their bane out of the north (as had been foretold, Jer 1:14-15), scil., from Babylon. And now Babylon is to be baned from the same quarter. This was some comfort, doubtless, to the poor Jews in captivity.
paragraphs.anchor: For out of the north there cometh up a nation against her

paragraphs.text: This was not fulfilled till many years after. Cyrus indeed began it, but Seleucus Nicanor finished it, by building near unto it another great city called Seleucia. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Which shall make her land desolate.

paragraphs.text: {a} Plin., lib. vi. cap. 26.
Destructio Babel salus est populo Dei; so shall it be at the ruin of Rome.
paragraphs.anchor: In those days, and at that time.

paragraphs.text: In better times they could not agree; but when they were both in a weeping condition, misery bred unity, as it did also between Hooper and Ridley, when they were both in prison for the truth.
paragraphs.anchor: The children of Israel shall come, and the children of Judah together.

paragraphs.text: Tears of sorrow for their sins, and tears of joy for their deliverance by Cyrus, but especially by Christ.
paragraphs.anchor: Going and weeping.

paragraphs.text: Whom they had long been without, and do now long and linger after.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall go and seek the Lord their God.

paragraphs.text: {a} As intent upon it, and minding nothing else in comparison. It is good for a man to have his face set towards heaven, and to make religion his business, looking at other things by the by, and out at the eye’s end, as it were.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall ask the way to Zion with their faces thitherward

paragraphs.text: Be so joined to the Lord, so glued unto him, as to be one spirit with him in a conjugal perpetual covenant. {b}
paragraphs.anchor: Come and let us join ourselves to the Lord.

paragraphs.text: {a} Accurate sciscitabuntur.
{b} Indivulse adhaerebunt Domino.
Per avis peccatorum aberrantes; lost in the maze of sin and misery.
paragraphs.anchor: My people have been lost sheep.

paragraphs.text: True also of Papists and sectaries, miserably misled by their pretended pastors - impostors rather.
paragraphs.anchor: Their shepherds have caused them to go astray.

paragraphs.text: As ravenous creatures do wandering sheep. Stragglers are a fit prey for seducers.
paragraphs.anchor: All that found them have devoured them.

paragraphs.text: i.e., God will have it so; {Jer 40:2} but this was no good plea. {Jer 2:3}
paragraphs.anchor: And their adversaries said, We offend not

paragraphs.text: Or, In the habitation of justice; in a land of uprightness have they dealt unjustly, {Isa 26:10} which was no small aggravation of their sin.
paragraphs.anchor: The habitation of justice.

paragraphs.text: But these, as degenerate children, have no such hope.
paragraphs.anchor: Even the Lord, the hope of their fathers.

paragraphs.text: "Ho, ho, come forth." {as Zec 2:6} "Away, this is not your rest, for it is polluted." {Mic 2:10} See Isa 48:20 Rev 18:4.
paragraphs.anchor: Remove out of the midst of Babylon.

paragraphs.text: That lead the flocks, generose et festinanter, freely and readily. Sheep are fearful, and therefore go behind; goats are not so, and therefore go before. There is good hope, saith one, that we are going out of Babylon, when the he-goats go before the flock; when men of public place and authority are active for reformation.
paragraphs.anchor: Be as the he-goats.

paragraphs.text: See on Jer 50:3.
paragraphs.anchor: From the north country.

paragraphs.text: Or, Of a potent prosperous man, that can hit where he pleaseth, and that without fail.
paragraphs.anchor: Their arrows shall be as a mighty expert man.

paragraphs.text: No shaft shall, or no soldier shall miss of booty; for whereas Babylon, like a sea, had taken in the wealth of all nations, so it was meet that it should be exhausted, like as Rome was by the Goths and Vandals, and as Constantinople was by the Turks and Tartars.
paragraphs.anchor: None shall return in vain.

paragraphs.text: See on Jer 50:9.
paragraphs.anchor: And Chaldea shall be a spoil.

paragraphs.text: {a} scil., In a thing of naught, {as Amo 6:13} and in the miseries of my people ye were madly merry; therefore shall ye be let bleed in the vena cava, hollow vein.
paragraphs.anchor: Because ye were glad, because ye rejoiced

paragraphs.text: Ye have laughed yourselves fat, you have fatted yourselves as in a day of slaughter or of good cheer. It was at a feast that Babylon was taken.
paragraphs.anchor: Because ye are grown fat.

paragraphs.text: Or, Neigh as steeds, lusty steeds.
paragraphs.anchor: And bellow as bulls.

paragraphs.text: {a} Causam ponit petulantiam et dicacitatem. - Oecol.

i.e., Babylon, your mother city, or Babylonia, your country; or your monarchical greatness, which being in the last place laid waste after other nations, {as Jer 25:25-26 was foretold} shall with shame cry out, Heu tam cito me quae primas obtinebam, &c. How is it that I, who was the head of nations, am now the tail, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: Your mother shall be sore confounded

paragraphs.text: Babylon standeth not now in the same place as of old, nor is there hardly any ruins of the old city remaining, as travellers tell us. Pausanias saith that in his time there was nought to be seen of it but the walls only; and Jerome saith {a} that in his it was turned into a park for deer. Omne in medio spatium solitude est. See on Jer 50:3.
paragraphs.anchor: It shall not be inhabited, but be wholly desolate.

paragraphs.text: {a} Lib. viii. in Isa. xiii.

Yea, she is a sink of sins, the contagion of the world, the shop of Satan, the adversary of the saints, &c. So, and much more than so, is spiritual Babylon, Cito itidem casura, ei essetis viri (said Petrarch long since), that groaneth for a downfall.
paragraphs.anchor: For she hath sinned against the Lord.

paragraphs.text: As they did once at Jericho; she shall come down assuredly.
paragraphs.anchor: Shout against her round about.

paragraphs.text: {a} i.e., She hath yielded, and cried quarter; add hereunto that two princes of Babylon, being displeased by Belshazzar, sent for Cyrus to take the city, and showed him how he might best do it. This was "giving the hands" saith Calvin.
paragraphs.anchor: She hath given her hand

paragraphs.text: Neque enim lex iustior ulla est. See Jdg 1:5. {See Trapp on "Jdg 1:5"}
paragraphs.anchor: As she hath done, do unto her.

paragraphs.text: {a} Deditionis est signum. Dare manus est fateri ae victum.
“ Victum tendere palmas
Ausanii videre. ” - Virg.

Leave not so much as a husbandman alive, who yet are generally spared, as harmless and useful; they were left and let alone by the Chaldeans when they carried away the Jews. {2Ki 25:12} But here is enjoined a more severe execution.
paragraphs.anchor: Cut off the sower.

paragraphs.text: Many Assyrian kings successively, but especially Sennacherib.
paragraphs.anchor: First the king of Assyria hath devoured him.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Hath boned him hath left nothing of him but the bare bones.
paragraphs.anchor: Hath broken his bones.

paragraphs.text: And accordingly so he did; for as Sennacherib first lost his army, and then his life, and then soon after that monarchy was dissolved; so after that Belshazzar was slain, the empire was translated unto the Persians.
paragraphs.anchor: As I have punished the king of Assyria.

paragraphs.text: Or, To his fold, or his pastures. See Jer 50:6; Jer 50:17.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will bring Israel again to his habitation.

paragraphs.text: Because to the justified no sin is imputed. Nihil oblivisci solet praeter iniurias. He forgetteth nothing but injuries only, said Cicero of Caesar, flatteringly, say we of God truly. This to have known is to feed in those soul fatting pastures. {Jer 50:19}
paragraphs.anchor: The iniquity of Jacob shall be sought for, and there shall be none.

paragraphs.text: Tegam quod fuit; quod erit, regam. I will cover what was; which will be, for I will rule.
paragraphs.anchor: For I will pardon them whom I reserve.

paragraphs.text: Two Babylonian provinces. {Eze 23:23} Calvin rendereth it, The land of exasperators, and the inhabitation of visitation, i.e., that deserve to be punished. This is God’s commission to Cyrus.
paragraphs.anchor: Go up against the land of Merathaim, and against the inhabitants of Pekod.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Their posterity. {as Dan 4:11}
paragraphs.anchor: Utterly destroy after them

paragraphs.text: Barrites militaris; this is, not the joyful, but the woeful sound; for war is a woe which no words, however wide, can sufficiently set forth. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: A sound of battle is in the land.

paragraphs.text: {a} Sequitur executio. - Oecol.

Babylon was the maul or hammer of many nations, Nimrod began it, and his successors took after him. Charles Martel, King of France, was so called for like cause. Augustine also was worthily styled Haereticorum malleus, the hammer of heretics; and Mr Arthur Hildersam, Schismaticorum malleus, the maul of schismatics.
paragraphs.anchor: How is the hammer of the whole earth cut asunder!

paragraphs.text: Thou wild bull. {Jer 50:27} Babylon was unexpectedly taken by a stratagem, while they were in the midst of their revels.
paragraphs.anchor: I have laid a snare for thee.

paragraphs.text: The palace was suddenly seized upon; but some parts of the city knew not that the enemy was entered till three days after; for it was the greatest city that ever the sun beheld, saith Pausanias, {a} and the most suddenly surprised.
paragraphs.anchor: And thou wast not aware.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Hast mingled thyself with the Lord, in certamen scilicet, to wrestle a fall with him, and to try masteries.
paragraphs.anchor: Because thou hast striven against the Lord.

paragraphs.text: {a} Aristot., Polit., Paus., Arcad.

Heb., Treasury. Now God’s armoury is omne id sub coelo, usque ad diabolos; all things, both in heaven and under the cope of heaven, as far as the very devils, whereby he is able to subdue his enemies, and to bring them to nothing. Out of this treasury God took Darius and Cyrus, with their forces, and set them upon this expedition.
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord hath opened his armoury.

paragraphs.text: This he speaketh to the Medes and Persians, who, though they were farther remote than they that could hear the prophet, yet God, who spake by him, could and did speak home to their hearts, stirring them up by a secret instinct to do this execution.
paragraphs.anchor: Come against her.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Sword them, sheath your swords in their sides. See Jer 50:24.
paragraphs.anchor: Slay all her bullocks.

paragraphs.text: Spoiled and burnt by the Chaldeans, those wasters, as their name also signifieth. Woe, then, to such as destroy God’s living temples!
paragraphs.anchor: The vengeance of his temple.

paragraphs.text: See Jer 50:15.
paragraphs.anchor: According to all that she hath done.

paragraphs.text: Who setteth himself in battle array against the proud. {1Pe 5:5}
paragraphs.anchor: For she hath been proud against the Lord.

paragraphs.text: See on Jer 49:26.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore shall her young men.

paragraphs.text: Heb., O pride, in the abstract - i.e., O Belshazzar; as of a certain Pope was said,
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, I am against thee, O most proud.

paragraphs.text: “ Conditur hoc tumulo et scelus et vitium. ”
Heb., Pride, or that man of pride. Praefractarius ille, so Oecolampadius rendereth it, that stubborn man, who will do wickedly against conviction of conscience.
paragraphs.anchor: And the most proud shall stumble.

paragraphs.text: Or, Were oppressed alike - scil., in their several deportations; and God, mindful of his covenant, showeth himself sensible of it, though for the present he seemed not to care what became of either of them; -
paragraphs.anchor: The children of Judah and the children of Israel were oppressed together.

paragraphs.text: “ Ille dolet quoties cogitur esse ferox. ”
Or, But their strong avenger, whose name is the Lord of hosts; he shall thoroughly plead their cause - i.e., right their wrongs.
paragraphs.anchor: Their Redeemer is strong.

paragraphs.text: See on 2Th 1:8-9.
paragraphs.anchor: That he may give rest to the land.

paragraphs.text: Those sworn swordsmen of the devil.
paragraphs.anchor: A sword is upon the Chaldeans.

paragraphs.text: i.e., The prognosticators and wizards. Mendaces nominat divines, as it was wont here to be said - a friar, a liar.
paragraphs.anchor: A sword is upon the liars

paragraphs.text: Upon all their military preparations; whereof see Herodot., lib. i.
paragraphs.anchor: A sword is upon their horses.

paragraphs.text: Elumbes, cowardly and crest fallen.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall become as women.

paragraphs.text: Which bow inestimable they were, see Strabo, lib. xv., and Plin., lib. xxxiii, cap. 3.
paragraphs.anchor: A sword is upon her treasures.

paragraphs.text: Which Cyrus did so drain by many outlets, that without any great difficulty he took the city, assaulting it on two sides. Frontinius saith, {a} that thrice Babylon was taken by this stratagem; (1.) By Semiramis; (2.) By Cyrus; (3.) By Alexander the Great.
paragraphs.anchor: A drought is upon her waters.

paragraphs.text: {b} Deos terrificos et truces, statues of their kings and worthies, which were of a huge, vast stature. See Dan 3:1.
paragraphs.anchor: And they are mad upon their idols.

paragraphs.text: {a} Lib. iii. c. 7. s. 4.
{b} ειδωλομανεις.
See Isa 13:21.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore the wild beasts of the desert.

paragraphs.text: See Isa 13:19 Jer 49:18.
paragraphs.anchor: As God overthrew Sodom.

paragraphs.text: As Jer 50:3; Jer 50:9; Jer 6:22.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, a people shall come from the north.

paragraphs.text: In like sort as thou didst once against God’s Israel. {Jer 6:23} Now thou shalt meet with thy match.
paragraphs.anchor: Against thee, O daughter of Babylon.

paragraphs.text: See Jer 6:24 Dan 5:6.
paragraphs.anchor: The king of Babylon, &c.

paragraphs.text: See Jer 49:19.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, he shall come up.

paragraphs.text: See on Jer 49:20.
